table1.note: SisFall trials annotated as 19 activities of daily living (2,702 trials) and 15 fall types (1,798 trials), two IMUs at 200 Hz. Windows: 1 s, 50% overlap; a fall-trial window is positive only if it overlaps the impact (peak resultant acceleration +/- 0.25 s), other fall-trial windows are kept as hard negatives.

table2.note: Leave-one-subject-out protocol pooled over 38 folds (window level). Recall@5%FPR: fall recall when the false-positive rate is fixed at 5%. CIs are subject-level bootstrap (500 resamples).

table3.note: Leave-one-fall-type-out: the detector is trained with one of the 15 fall types entirely absent and tested on it at the same 5% false-positive operating point (threshold from ADL windows scored by the same model). Fall types: F01-F03 slip while walking; F04-F07 fainting while walking; F08-F10 falls when trying to sit; F11-F13 falls when trying to stand; F14-F15 vertical/forward fainting falls.

table4.note: Cross-age deployment test. SisFall's falls were simulated by the 23 young subjects; the 15 elderly subjects performed daily activities only (SE06 is the single exception, contributing 15 fall trials). Threshold: 95th percentile of the LOSO score on young ADL windows. All values from results/age_transfer.csv.

table5.note: Device-position transfer: the same gradient-boosting protocol restricted to the features of one body-worn unit (waist ADXL345 vs chest MMA8451Q), leave-one-subject-out.
